title: Chromatin and transcription factor profiling in rare stem cell populations using CUT and Tag
protocol: Euthanize the mice using CO2 chamber, and sterilize the mice with 70% ethanol.
Isolate the CTX-injured TA and gastroc muscles.
Transfer the muscles from one mouse into a 10 cm dish containing 15 mL of PBS pre-warmed to 37°C.
Rinse the muscles in the dish.
Transfer the muscles to a new 10 cm dish with at least 15 mL of PBS pre-warmed to 37°C.
Rinse the muscles again in the dish.
Transfer the muscles into a new 6 cm dish with PBS.
Aspirate PBS from the muscle sample.
Mince the muscle sample into approximately 1 mm³ pieces using dissection scissors.
Add Collagenase I/Dispase II solution to the 6 cm dish containing minced muscle.
Incubate the dish at 37°C for 1 hour in a cell culture incubator.
Shake the dish every 15 minutes during incubation.
Coat pipettes, 50 mL conical tubes, and strainers with Bovine Growth Serum/Calf Serum while waiting for digestion completion.
Coat all pipets, conical tubes, and strainers with BGS before use.
Aspirate BGS up to full capacity of the pipet and flush out. Repeat twice more for thorough coating.
Add 5 mL BGS into a 50 mL conical tube, rock and invert to ensure BGS contacts entire inner surface.
Place a strainer onto a 50 mL conical tube and flush BGS over it to coat the entire surface of the strainer.
After 1 hour of digestion, use BGS-coated pipets to triturate muscle pieces by pipetting up and down until a homogeneous mixture is generated in the dish.
Add 5 mL BGS into the digested sample and mix by pipetting to dilute collagenase I and stop tissue digestion.
Use a 100 μm strainer to strain the digested muscle sample into a 50 mL conical tube.
Rinse the 6 cm dish with PBS heated to 37°C to collect residual cells.
Run the PBS through a strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Repeat rinsing and straining one or two times more to ensure all cells are collected.
Filter the 100 μm-strained sample using a 40 μm strainer into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the filtered sample at 300 × g for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant and add 500 μL of red blood cell lysis buffer to the pellet in the 50 mL conical tube.
Pipette up and down to resuspend the pellet.
Wait for 1 minute, then add 10 mL of FACS buffer into the 50 mL conical tube.
Rock to mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 7 minutes at room temperature.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Transfer the sample to a microcentrifuge tube.
Filter the 1 mL muscle tissue-derived cell mixture into a 5-mL Polypropylene round bottom FACS tube using CellTrics 50 μm filters.
Pass 1 mL of FACS buffer through the same filter to bring up the sample volume to 4 mL.
Add 2 mL of FACS buffer to the tube.
Place the sample on ice and add SYTOX™ Green nucleic acid stain (final concentration: 10 nM) into the sample to stain dead cells.
Collect sorted MuSCs in a microcentrifuge tube containing 300–400 μL FACS buffer without EDTA.
Add cell surface marker antibodies to 1 mL FACS buffer containing the cell mixture.
Incubate on a rotator at 4°C for 30 min, protected from light.
Spin down the cells at 300×g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell mixture with 500 μL FACS buffer.
Add 5 μL Streptavidin-PE and incubate on a rotator at room temperature for 5 min, protected from light.
Spin down the cells at 300×g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the loose pellet in 200 μL of FACS buffer.
Add 10 μL of 7-AAD and incubate on ice protected from light for 2 min.
Dilute the cell mixture by adding 800 μL FACS buffer.
Filter the cell mixture through CellTrics 50 μm filters.
Bring up the sample volume to 4 mL by passing 1 mL of FACS buffer through the filter and then by adding 2 mL FACS buffer into the tube.
Place the sample on ice and proceed for FACS sorting.
Collect sorted MuSCs in a microcentrifuge tube containing 300–400 μL FACS buffer without EDTA.
Incubate 50,000 MuSCs with 20 μL of BioMag®Plus Concanavalin A bead solution in a microcentrifuge tube.
Pool muscles from more than one mouse if necessary to obtain sufficient number of cells for CUT&Tag reactions.
FACS-sort pooled muscle tissue before separating into distinct CUT&Tag reactions.
Ensure the same number of MuSCs (50,000) is used per CUT&Tag reaction across all conditions being tested.
Shake or invert the bottle containing Concanavalin A bead solution several times to thoroughly mix the contents.
Aspirate 90 μL of BioMag®Plus Concanavalin A bead solution into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube containing 850 μL Binding buffer.
Mix the binding buffer with Concanavalin A beads in the 1.5 mL tube by mild-pipetting or by inverting and tapping.
Place on a magnetic rack and let it sit for 2 min to be clear.
Withdraw the buffer and then remove the tube from the magnetic rack.
Add 800 μL Binding buffer into the tube.
Completely resuspend the beads by mild-pipetting or by inverting and tapping.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack and let it sit for 2 min to be clear.
Remove the liquid completely from the microcentrifuge tube containing FACS-sorted MuSCs.
Take the tube off the magnetic rack.
Resuspend the beads in 90 μL of binding buffer.
Spin down the microcentrifuge tube containing FACS-sorted MuSCs at 600×g for 5 min at 22°C.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant from the cell pellet without touching or aspirating the cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 750 μL of wash buffer.
Add the 90 μL of Concanavalin A bead slurry dropwise to the tube containing cells while gently vortexing.
Place the tube on an end-to-end rotator at 22°C for 15 min.
Place the microcentrifuge tube on a magnetic rack and let it sit for 2 min until clear.
Transfer the liquid (supernatant) to a new microcentrifuge tube.
Proceed with the Concanavalin A beads-MuSCs cell mixture to step 31.
Drop 5-10 μL of supernatant into one of the chambers of a hemocytometer and observe under the microscope for cells.
Dilute the primary antibody in 100 μL of antibody buffer at double the working concentration required for immunofluorescence microscopy studies.
Add the diluted primary antibody into microcentrifuge tubes containing a 100 μL cell-bead mixture, resulting in the final antibody concentration equivalent to that used in immunofluorescence.
Place the tubes on a nutator at 4°C and agitate overnight.
Flick or briefly spin the tubes after agitation to remove beads from the cap and walls.
Place the tubes on a magnetic rack for 2 minutes and remove the primary antibody liquid.
Add 200 μL of Digitonin-wash buffer containing secondary antibody diluted at 1:100 into each tube.
Remove the tubes from the magnetic rack, vortex mildly at 300 rpm, and nutate them at 22°C for 1 hour.
Flick or briefly spin the tubes after nutation and place them on a magnetic rack for 2 minutes to remove the secondary antibody liquid.
Wash the cell-bead mixture by adding 200 μL of Digitonin-wash buffer into each tube.
Close the caps, remove the tubes from the magnetic rack, invert the tubes 20 times, quick spin to remove liquid from cap, and place back onto a magnetic rack for 2 minutes.
Remove the Digitonin-wash buffer from the tubes after washing.
Repeat steps of adding 200 μL Digitonin-wash buffer, closing caps, inverting, quick spinning, and placing on magnetic rack for an additional wash.
Dilute pA-Tn5 fusion protein to 1:250 using Digitonin-300 wash buffer to achieve a final concentration of 18.96 nM.
Add 100 μL of the diluted pA-Tn5 fusion protein into each tube.
Nutate tubes for 1 hour at 22°C after removing them from the magnetic rack.
Flick or briefly spin the tubes and place them back on the magnetic rack.
Wait for 2 minutes, then remove the pA-Tn5 containing liquid.
Wash the cell-bead mixture by adding 800 μL of Digitonin-300 wash buffer to each tube.
Invert the tubes 10–20 times and quick spin to remove liquid from cap.
Place the tubes back onto the magnetic rack and wait for 2 minutes.
Remove the Digitonin-300 wash buffer from the tubes.
Repeat washing step three times using Digitonin-300 wash buffer.
Add 300 μL of Tagmentation buffer containing Spike-inAmpR (0.1899 amol/L) to each CUT&Tag reaction tube.
Invert or tap the tubes to mix well.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Add 10 μL of 0.5 M EDTA, 3 μL of 10% SDS, and 2.5 μL of 20 mg/mL Proteinase K to each tube.
Vortex the tubes to mix well.
Incubate at 37°C overnight or for 1 hour at 55°C.
Add 300 μL of Phenol/Chloroform into each tube.
Vortex thoroughly.
Transfer the contents to a freshly labeled phase lock tube and centrifuge at 16,000×g for 5 minutes.
Transfer the aqueous layer to a new labeled microcentrifuge tube.
Add 300 μL of chloroform into each new tube.
Invert to mix thoroughly.
Spin the tubes at 16,000×g for 5 minutes.
Transfer the aqueous layer to a fresh new tube.
Label the new tubes accordingly and properly.
Add 1 μL of 20 mg/mL glycogen solution into each tube.
Vortex.
Add 750 μL of 100% ethanol into each tube.
Invert several times.
Place at −80°C to precipitate the tagmented DNA.
Thaw samples on ice.
Spin microcentrifuge tubes at maximum speed for 15 minutes using a benchtop centrifuge at 4°C.
Pour off liquid and add 1 mL of 100% ethanol into each tube.
Invert several times to wash the pellet.
Spin tubes again at 18,000×g for 10 minutes in a benchtop microcentrifuge.
Carefully pour off the ethanol from the tubes.
Wipe off residual ethanol from the cap and edge of the tubes using Kimwipes.
Dry tubes completely in a fume hood with caps open to remove any residual ethanol.
Add 25 μL CUT&Tag DNA resuspension Buffer into each tube.
Incubate at 37°C for 10 minutes to dissolve the pellet.
Aliquot 2 μL from each CUT&Tagged genomic DNA sample.
Dilute the Spike-inAmpR fragment to a concentration of 65.6 nM.
Set up qPCR on AmpR gene fragment using specified conditions.
Calculate the standard qPCR reaction concentration: 65.6 nM × (2/25) = 5.25 nM.
Set up qPCR on each aliquoted 2 μL CUT&Tagged genomic DNA sample using specified conditions.
Run the standard qPCR reaction along with CUT&Tagged genomic DNA samples using cycling parameters.
Record the cycle numbers required by each sample to reach a fluorescence intensity equivalent to that observed in the Spike-inAmpR control at 5 cycles.
Set up the actual library preparation using 20 μL of each CUT&Tagged genomic DNA sample.
Perform PCR cycling as per the conditions provided for actual library preparation.
Determine optimal number of cycles for "Denaturation" and "Annealing and extension" steps at step 55.
Adapt the cycle numbers based on the determination from step 55.
Reduce optimized cycle numbers by 2 cycles for actual library preparation PCR.
Use different i5 and/or i7 primers to distinguish samples sequenced in the same lane.
Recommend using 12 different i7 primers for sample distinction.
Recommend using 8 different i5 primers for sample distinction.
Generate a combination of 96 distinct primer sets (8 x 12).
Ensure sufficient differentiation among up to 30-40 pooled samples per sequencing lane.
Aliquot 3–5 μL of the library from a total volume of 50 μL.
Purify the aliquoted library using QIAquick PCR Purification Kit.
Elute the purified library in 40 μL of H2O.
Set up qPCR diagnosis using locus-specific primers to test for antibody-targeted enrichment.
Use IgG as negative control.
Use H3K4me3 antibody (Millipore) as positive control.
Amplify Gapdh locus using forward primer CTCTGAGCCTCCTCCAATTC and reverse primer GCTACGCCATAGGTCAGGAT.
Amplify a mouse gene-desert region using forward primer TCCTCCCCATCTGTGTCATC and reverse primer GGATCCATCACCATCAATAACC.
Ensure the amplification of Gapdh locus in H3K4me3 CUT&Tag sample is at least 3 cycles ahead of IgG sample.
Confirm that the gene-desert primer does not significantly amplify more tagmented DNA from H3K4me3 antibody sample compared to IgG sample.
Mix 45 μL of PCR-prepared library with 63 μL Kapa Pure beads in an Axygen microcentrifuge tube.
Pipette few times to get this fully mixed.
Quickly spin down the mixture and keep at room temperature for 10 min.
Place the microcentrifuge tube on a magnetic rack and wait till clear.
Withdraw the liquid from the tubes and avoid disturbing the beads.
Wash twice by adding 200 μL 80% ethanol in the tube.
Return the tube to the magnetic rack and withdraw the liquid from the tube.
Remove the residual liquid from the tube by pipetting.
Wait for 5 min to dry the beads.
Add 21 μL of 10 mM Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) to the tube.
Vortex to fully mix.
Wait for 5 min and put the tubes back onto the magnetic rack.
Wait till clear and transfer the liquid to a fresh tube.
The liquid contains the cleaned-up DNA for sequencing.
Quantify sample concentration using a Qubit™ 1× dsDNA HS Assay as per the manufacturer’s guide.
Adjust the sample to a concentration of 4 ng/μL using 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 8 for dilution if necessary.
Assess the quality of the tagmented DNA library using Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity DNA Analysis (Agilent).
Load a sample dilution at 2 ng/μL on the Chip when possible.
If the sample concentration is below 2 ng/μL, load the sample undiluted.
Determine the library size using the average size value for a region between 170 bp to 1000 bp.
Determine the final sample concentration for sequencing using NEBNext® Library Quant Kit for Illumina.
Run samples according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Pool and sequence samples on NovaSeq 6000 or equivalent platform using 50 bp Paired-End sequencing at approximately 10 M per sample.
Use a S1 flowcell on an XP workflow but note that any flowcell type can be used (SP, S1, S2, S4) and any workflow (standard or regular).
Analyze sequencing data using the CUT&Tag pipeline established in Github.
Perform quality control of raw FASTQ reads.
Trim adapters from sequences.
Align reads to primary genome and spike-in sequences.
Filter aligned sequences post-alignment.
Normalize samples using Spike-inAmpR as default.
Call peaks from processed data.
Prepare the software environment and download the data.
Install FastQC v0.11.9.
Install MultiQC >=1.9.
Install Cutadapt >=2.6.
Install Bowtie2 >=2.4.1.
Install Samtools >=1.11.
Install Picard Tools >= 2.22.5.
Install deepTools >=3.3.2.
Install SEACR >=1.3.
Install BEDtools >= 2.29.2.
Install bedToBigBed >= 2.7.
Install ChIPseeker >= 1.24.0.
Download raw FASTQ reads to desired location.
Perform md5sum checks to verify the integrity of all files.
Run FastQC on each raw FASTQ read individually.
Perform preliminary quality control checks using FastQC results.
Proceed with further analysis even if the library does not pass all QC modules defined by FastQC.
Remake the library if there is a fail in the “per base sequence quality” score.
Analyze non-uniform base composition at the start of reads due to Tn5 transposition bias.
Mix CTGTCTCTTATACACATCT adapter sequences with reads using Cutadapt in paired-end mode.
Output trimmed reads as Trim.R1 and Trim.R2 files.
Align trimmed paired-end reads to the Mus musculus or Homo sapiens genome using Bowtie2.
Pipe Bowtie2 output directly to Samtools for conversion into BAM format.
Sort resulting BAM files by coordinates using Samtools.
Index coordinate-sorted BAM files using Samtools.
Run MultiQC in a directory containing the appropriate log files.
Filter resulting BAM files to retain mapped and properly paired reads using Samtools flag -f2.
Perform MAPQ-based filtering with Samtools flag -q 10 to keep only uniquely aligned reads.
Mark and remove duplicates from filtered BAM files using MarkDuplicates from Picard.

Calculate normalization factors for each sample by dividing the number of spike-in reads in a reference sample (Spikemin) by the number of total mapped reads in the sample being normalized (Spikesample).
Use bamCoverage from deepTools to obtain spike-in normalized bigwig and bedgraph files, applying appropriate scale factor based on calculated normalization factors.
Upload generated BigWig files for visualization on the UCSC genome browser.
